1508: Two mirrored walls multiply the chip aisle into forever. One customer walks deeper past endless identical cats, the exit sign a distant star
1509: Through the brass fisheye the landing curves like a snow globe. A neighbor mid knock, holding soup
1510: The neon runs like wet paint down the night glass. One clear drop holds the whole skyline sharp inside it
1511: One family stretched tall, wide, wavy, and tiny, all four reflections laughing differently. Grandpa finally taller than his brother
1512: The chalk canyon is so convincing pedestrians step around it. One fearless kid stands in its center on flat ground while commuters teeter at the painted edge
1513: A painted window, a painted cat, painted geraniums on the brick. The real cat next door studies its flat rival, pigeons refusing the fake ledge on principle
1514: A thousand tiny cities in its mirrors, each facet a different block. One facet holds a rooftop where someone dances alone
1515: The dawn shadow is already at the corner, already taller, already arriving. The small person walks calmly behind their own future
1516: Stuck at 4:19 for thirty years, right twice a day and beloved always. A commuter checks it anyway out of loyalty, pigeons roosting on the minute hand
